name: Campomelic Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Campomelic Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of bowed and shortened long bones, especially tibiae and femora
46,XY sex reversal or ambiguous genitalia in genetic males
Severe respiratory distress due to tracheobronchomalacia or hypoplastic thorax
Characteristic facial features including flat face, micrognathia, and cleft palate

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bowed long bones and respiratory complications plus identification of SOX9 mutation or clinical sex reversal in 46,XY individuals
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for SOX9 mutations is confirmatory; clinical diagnosis relies on skeletal and respiratory findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe respiratory distress due to tracheobronchomalacia

common.symptomName: Hypoplastic thorax leading to restrictive lung disease
Facial dysmorphism including flat face and micrognathia

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac malformations such as septal defects
Respiratory infections secondary to airway malacia

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; genetic testing reveals SOX9 mutations
imaging: Radiographs showing bowed and shortened long bones
MRI or ultrasound may show hydrocephalus or other CNS anomalies
genetic: Heterozygous mutations in SOX9 gene, often de novo
other: Clinical examination reveals ambiguous genitalia in 46,XY individuals
Respiratory function tests show restrictive lung disease

distinguishingFeatures: Extreme micromelia with telephone receiver femora

redFlags: Progressive respiratory failure due to thoracic hypoplasia
references: Wagner T, Wirth J, Meyer J, et al. Autosomal sex reversal and campomelic dysplasia are caused by mutations in and around the SRY-related gene SOX9. Cell. 1994.
Foster JW, Dominguez-Steglich MA, Guioli S, et al. Campomelic dysplasia and autosomal sex reversal caused by mutations in an SRY-related gene. Nature. 1994.
Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2019 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
